items.title: 33 of 45 local data center ballot measures will restrict building
items.takeaway: NBC polling found 76% oppose data centers locally; Ohio and Kansas towns passed size bans.
items.soWhat: Local votes now shape where compute gets built, so stress-test capacity plans against delays.

items.title: AI agents booked just four Uber rides last quarter
items.takeaway: Uber's first agent disclosure: about 500 Eats orders in Halloween week, against 320 million trips and deliveries.
items.soWhat: Agent commerce is still tiny, so don't rebuild sales channels around it yet.

items.title: Moonshot releases open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.takeaway: 2.8T-parameter model, 1M-token context; vendor reports Terminal-Bench 65.7 vs Claude Opus 5.5's 66.4.
items.soWhat: Near-frontier coding models you can host yourself give you leverage in vendor pricing talks.

image.alt: Image from Hugging Face model card

items.title: Meng To has Claude score screenshots of its own 3D site
items.takeaway: A 13-minute video; he says the self-review loop lifted a 4.6 score past 8.
items.soWhat: Letting the model check its own output against a target is a cheap way to raise design quality.

items.title: Altman walks back his remark about RAM in personal computers
items.takeaway: He now says people should have as much memory as they want; Intel expects the shortage through next year.
items.soWhat: AI data centers are absorbing memory supply, so expect pricier laptops and servers into 2027.

items.title: Builders argue agent-written code needs verifiability more than readability
items.takeaway: Pocock: make modules testable on their own; poteto says his team ships 30x more code unread.
items.soWhat: Invest in tests and checks agents can run, since fewer people will read the code.

items.title: Matt Pocock weighs shipping his agent skills as versioned npm packages
items.takeaway: His skills repo had 312,813 GitHub stars; npm would let teams pin versions per agent.
items.soWhat: Agent skills are becoming dependencies, so manage them with version pinning and review.

items.title: Gemini can train on paid personal chats unless activity is off
items.takeaway: Turning off Keep Activity deletes chats after 72 hours; human-reviewed chats are kept up to three years.
items.soWhat: Staff using personal Gemini accounts may be feeding company data into model training.

image.alt: Hacker News: Gemini can train on paid personal chats unless activity is off

items.title: Hinton predicts a Chornobyl-scale AI incident by next year
items.takeaway: He cites a power brownout or week-long financial outage and backs mandatory testing of frontier models.
items.soWhat: Calls for mandatory model testing are growing, so plan for audits of the AI you deploy.

items.title: Scam websites fooled web agents 11% to 35% of the time
items.takeaway: ScamWorld tested agents on six frontier models; they paid more readily than they gave credentials.
items.soWhat: Don't let agents make payments without a human check or strict spending limits.

image.alt: arXiv 2611.04879: Scam websites fooled web agents 11% to 35% of the time

items.title: AI turned an ignored PHP crash into a critical exploit
items.takeaway: A 2024 crash report sat unfixed until an AI-aided audit made it remote code execution in two weeks.
items.soWhat: AI makes old, unpatched bugs exploitable fast, so legacy code now carries fresh risk.

items.title: RTX Spark laptops run local models five times slower on Linux
items.takeaway: MindStudio measured 13.9 tokens/s on native Linux vs 65.4 on Windows; WSL keeps full speed.
items.soWhat: Benchmark local AI hardware on the operating system your team will actually use.
